requirement_title: Add ExcludeFromCodeCoverage attribute to generated code.
requirement_text:
# REQ-2297: Add ExcludeFromCodeCoverage attribute to generated code.

Source: https://github.com/MessagePack-CSharp/MessagePack-CSharp/issues/2297
Type: feature

## Requirement

MessagePack generated code is not decorated with the `ExcludeFromCodeCoverage` attribute. Because it is very hard to write good coverage for generated MessagePack code, it may skew coverage numbers, especially on large projects with a lot of generated code.

Solution requested: "I would like all generated code to be decorated with ExcludeFromCodeCoverage attribute.  I do not feel like a setting is needed, but setting would be fine to have too."

Alternatives considered by the author: none; "it is close to impossible to write good coverage for generated code as it covers many edge cases."

## Acceptance criteria

- All generated code is decorated with `ExcludeFromCodeCoverage`.
- No new setting or option is required to get the attribute. ("I do not feel like a setting is needed")
- An opt-out setting would be acceptable but is optional. ("setting would be fine to have too")
- The generated code still compiles on every supported target framework (the attribute must exist there or be conditionally emitted). (derived)
- Existing verified generator snapshots are updated to include the attribute. (derived)

## Notes from discussion

- b-kurczynski-dl suggests a coverage-tool workaround instead: exclude `obj\\.*\.g\.cs$` in the `dotnet-coverage` settings XML.
- armadavalor offers a PR: add `[global::System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.ExcludeFromCodeCoverage]` (and possibly `GeneratedCode`) to the types emitted by the templates under `src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/Transforms/` (formatters, string-key formatters, enum/union formatters, resolvers), update the verified snapshots, no setting. Asks AArnott whether he would accept it or prefer to point users at coverage-tool configuration. No maintainer reply in the thread.
- Ambiguity driver: scope (all generated types vs formatters only) and setting (unconditional vs opt-out) are both open.

findings.claim: Not all generated code gets the attribute. Only the four formatter templates (object, string-key, enum, union) were changed. The generated resolver partial class, its nested helper/cache types, and composite resolver output come from untouched templates and carry no `ExcludeFromCodeCoverage`. The acceptance criterion says "All generated code is decorated", so resolver code still counts toward coverage.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAllScopeTests.AllGeneratedTypes_AreDecoratedWithExcludeFromCodeCoverage. On head it should fail and list the resolver type `MyResolver` (and its nested helper types) as undecorated.

findings.claim: Every changed template wraps the attribute in `#if !NETSTANDARD2_0 && !NETFRAMEWORK`. Consumers targeting netstandard2.0 or .NET Framework therefore get no attribute. Yet `System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute` exists on .NET Framework 4.0+ and netstandard2.0. The derived criterion allows conditional emission only where the attribute does not exist, so the guard drops the requirement for supported targets that have it.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAllScopeTests.FormatterTypes_AreDecorated_OnNetStandardAndNetFramework (NETSTANDARD2_0 and NETFRAMEWORK). It reparses the generated formatters with those preprocessor symbols. On head the attribute is in an inactive #if region and the test fails. The same guard appears in EnumTemplate.tt:8, StringKeyFormatterTemplate.tt:18 and UnionTemplate.tt:10.

findings.claim: Every template wraps the attribute in `#if !NETSTANDARD2_0 && !NETFRAMEWORK`, so it is dropped for netstandard2.0 and .NET Framework targets. Both targets do ship `System.Diagnostics.CodeAnalysis.ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute`: .NET Framework 4.0+ in System.dll, and netstandard2.0 in netstandard.dll, valid on Class. The guard is therefore unnecessary. A netstandard2.0 library (the most common MessagePack consumer target) gets no attribute, and its generated formatters still count toward coverage when net8 test projects exercise it. This breaks the 'all generated code is decorated' criterion.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.ExcludeFromCodeCoverageTargetSymbolTests.GeneratedFormatters_HaveExcludeFromCodeCoverage_WhenTargeting("NETSTANDARD2_0") and ("NETFRAMEWORK"). The test drives CSharpGeneratorDriver with that preprocessor symbol defined and asserts that every generated *Formatter class keeps the attribute. It fails on head because the attribute sits in disabled text. The same guard appears in EnumTemplate.tt:8, StringKeyFormatterTemplate.tt:18 and UnionTemplate.tt:10.

findings.claim: This change deletes a passing test (CodeCoverageExclusionTests.AllGeneratedTypesAreExcludedFromCodeCoverage, tests/MessagePack.SourceGenerator.Tests/CodeCoverageExclusionTests.cs:64 at a0aa5ab2de) that the ticket doesn't ask to remove. Other tests still run its lines, but nothing asserts what it asserted.

receipt_plan.detail: CodeCoverageExclusionTests.AllGeneratedTypesAreExcludedFromCodeCoverage passed at a0aa5ab2de (test-removal-1-before) and is absent on head

hunches.claim: The attribute is emitted only inside `#if !NETSTANDARD2_0 && !NETFRAMEWORK`. The `#if` is evaluated in the user's compilation, so on netstandard2.0, net472 and similar targets the formatters stay un-excluded and the attribute is missing. ExcludeFromCodeCoverage exists on net472 and netstandard2.0, so the guard is unnecessary, and the requirement says all generated code should be decorated. The condition also wrongly assumes those symbols are defined. Legacy projects that don't define NETFRAMEWORK, and multi-target projects, will get inconsistent results.

receipt_plan.detail: Build a netstandard2.0 or net472 consumer project with a [MessagePackObject] type. Inspect the generated formatter: the attribute is compiled out, so coverage is not excluded. Compare with a net8.0 build.

hunches.claim: The same guard on the enum, union and string-key templates leaves them un-excluded on netstandard2.0 and .NET Framework targets. The resolver and other generated types are not decorated in any visible hunk, so 'all generated code' is not covered. That includes the resolver, `GeneratedMessagePackResolver`, and the helper types the generator emits.

receipt_plan.detail: Run the snapshot tests, then grep the generated outputs for classes lacking ExcludeFromCodeCoverage: the resolver template and any other emitted types.

hunches.claim: The nesting-brace change from `{` to `{\r\n` alters the generated output for every formatter nested in a constrained generic or partial type. This is a whitespace-only change, but it shifts line positions and changes snapshots that users may check in. It is unrelated to the requirement. The `#if` directives are also emitted starting at column 0, directly after the `{`. If a preceding `{` had no newline, that would put `#if` mid-line and fail to compile. This fix is needed for that, but it shows the risk is real.

receipt_plan.detail: Rerun the snapshot tests for nested generic types with constraints. Confirm the nested-type snapshots changed only by the added newline and that the output compiles.

hunches.claim: Formatters are now decorated with an attribute that is unavailable on very old targets, and they are no longer byte-identical in generated output for users who check in or snapshot generated files. That diff is the explicit purpose of the requirement. However, `#if` directives in the output could trigger user-side analyzers or style rules (e.g. indentation or directive formatting), producing new warnings in builds with warnings-as-errors.

receipt_plan.detail: Compile the generated output under TreatWarningsAsErrors with the default analyzers across net472, netstandard2.0 and net8.0, and check that no new diagnostics appear.

hunches.claim: Requirement says ALL generated code must be decorated. The change decorates only formatter classes (object, string-key, enum, union). The generated resolver (GeneratedMessagePackResolver and its templates) and any other emitted types are not decorated. The README also says only 'generated formatters', so the scope is narrowed relative to the requirement.

receipt_plan.detail: Rerun generator snapshot tests and grep the generated resolver output (e.g. GeneratedMessagePackResolver.g.cs and resolver templates) for ExcludeFromCodeCoverage; expect it to be missing. Also extend CodeCoverageExclusionTests to include non-'Formatters.' files.

hunches.claim: The test only checks files whose names start with 'Formatters.', so the resolver output is never asserted. The test claims 'every formatter' but cannot detect undecorated resolver code. The Count>=4 assertion is also weak.

receipt_plan.detail: Remove the attribute from the resolver template emission, or add it nowhere; the tests still pass, showing the resolver is unchecked.

hunches.claim: The guard `#if !NETSTANDARD2_0 && !NETFRAMEWORK` is evaluated against the consumer's compilation symbols. The README claims behaviour for 'targets', but multi-target projects that define other symbols (e.g. UNITY, or older netcoreapp2.x / netcoreapp3.0 lacking the attribute before .NET 5) would still emit the attribute and fail to compile. The guard may be inexact, so the 'compiles on every supported target' criterion is not proven.

receipt_plan.detail: Compile generated output with a netcoreapp3.1 / Unity-like symbol set (no NETSTANDARD2_0 or NETFRAMEWORK defined) against a reference set lacking ExcludeFromCodeCoverage and assert no CS0234/CS0246.

hunches.claim: The TransformUtilities change from `{` to `{\r\n` alters the emitted output for nesting types with constraints. It is unrelated to the requirement and changes formatting in snapshots beyond the attribute.

receipt_plan.detail: Rerun snapshot tests and inspect snapshot diffs for nested generic-constraint types; changes unrelated to the attribute indicate scope creep.

hunches.claim: The tests only inspect files whose names start with "Formatters.". The resolver (GeneratedMessagePackResolver) and any other generated type are never checked. The requirement says all generated code, and the test comment claims every emitted formatter is covered. If the resolver is meant to be in scope, removing or never adding the attribute there would go unnoticed. The change also adds no attribute to the resolver template.

receipt_plan.detail: Extend the test to include non-Formatters.* generated trees (resolver) and assert the attribute. Expect failure, since the resolver template is unchanged in the diff.

hunches.claim: The first test asserts only that each file contains the attribute somewhere and that there are at least 4 files. A file with several formatters (for example nested types) is not checked per class, so deleting the attribute from one template while another formatter in the same file keeps it would survive. The count threshold of 4 is also weak. EnumTemplate, UnionTemplate, StringKey and Formatter may all be covered by separate files, but nothing ties each template to its own file.

receipt_plan.detail: src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/Transforms/UnionTemplate.cs:30 delete-statement: remove the ExcludeFromCodeCoverage line from the Write string -> expected to fail the test, but verify that the union file is among those enumerated. If the union formatter is not emitted under a Formatters.* path, the mutant survives.

hunches.claim: The guard condition `#if !NETSTANDARD2_0 && !NETFRAMEWORK` is checked only as a literal string. No test compiles the generated code against a netstandard2.0 or net472 target, or against a modern one, so the requirement that the generated code compiles on every target is unverified. The guard could be mutated to `#if NETSTANDARD2_0` and the second test would still pass if Guard were changed in step. Note that the Guard constant is duplicated in the test rather than derived.

receipt_plan.detail: EnumTemplate.cs:27 negate-condition: `#if !NETSTANDARD2_0 && !NETFRAMEWORK` -> `#if NETSTANDARD2_0`. The tests fail only on literal mismatch. A compile test with NETSTANDARD2_0 defined or undefined would catch it.

hunches.claim: The TransformUtilities change from "{" to "{\r\n" for nesting types with constraints alters generated output, but no test in the diff targets it. The new tests use no nested generic types with constraints. It is only covered indirectly through snapshots.

receipt_plan.detail: TransformUtilities.cs:58 swap-boolean/delete-statement: revert `{\r\n` -> `{`. Only the snapshot tests for nested generic constrained types would kill it. The new tests would not.

hunches.claim: Only the formatter templates (object, string-key, enum, union) receive the attribute. The resolver partial class and its nested helper or cache classes come from the resolver template, which is not touched. They remain without ExcludeFromCodeCoverage, so not all generated code is excluded from coverage.

receipt_plan.detail: No hunk modifies the resolver template under src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/Transforms/. Generate a resolver for `[GeneratedMessagePackResolver] partial class R {}` and check that the class declarations in MyNs.R.g.cs carry no ExcludeFromCodeCoverage attribute.

hunches.claim: The README note is placed in the custom-formatter/resolver section, not in a generator-focused section. It says 'All generated formatters' while the requirement says all generated code, and it states no opt-out.

receipt_plan.detail: Read README.md around line 1639 and compare against the requirement wording 'all generated code'.

refused.what: Which reading of REQ-2297 is intended (A or B)
refused.why: 3 of 3 independent readers found two readings: A: Unconditionally add [ExcludeFromCodeCoverage] to every type the source generator emits (formatters, enum/union formatters, resolvers, string-key formatters, etc.), with no setting; B: Add the attribute to all generated types by default, plus provide an opt-out setting (e.g. MSBuild property or MessagePackKnownFormatter/GeneratorOptions flag) to disable it; the requirement says: 'I would like all generated code to be decorated with ExcludeFromCodeCoverage attribute. I do not feel like a setting is needed, but setting would be fine to have too'.

residual_risk: This change touches 142 files (131 generated) in codegen-templates, tests; the highest routed risk is 8/10. 10 file(s) were routed for deep review, 1 for light review and 131 to the regeneration check. The existing source generator tests ran on head: 169 of 169 passed, 0 failed. 14 unverified hunch(es) remain without an executed receipt. It touches risky areas (codegen-templates), so a human must sign off. It modifies 5 existing member(s) that 10 call site(s) outside the change rely on; 0 of those call sites are not exercised by any test, and characterization tests showed 0 behaviour change(s). 7 thing(s) were not checked, including mutation testing; generated formatter bytes (source generator output, base vs head); compatibility byte diff (base vs head serialized bytes). By signing off, the signer accepts any defect that only those unchecked paths would have revealed. The change is blocked; signing off is not offered until the blocker is fixed.

interpretations.label: A
interpretations.summary: Unconditionally add [ExcludeFromCodeCoverage] to every type the source generator emits (formatters, enum/union formatters, resolvers, string-key formatters, etc.), with no setting. Code: Edit all templates under Transforms/ to emit the attribute on every generated type, always, with no MSBuild property or option; update all snapshots.

interpretations.label: B
interpretations.summary: Add the attribute to all generated types by default, plus provide an opt-out setting (e.g. MSBuild property or MessagePackKnownFormatter/GeneratorOptions flag) to disable it. Code: Adds a new public configuration option, reads it in the generator, and conditionally emits the attribute in templates; the other reading adds no option.
